The stakes are high. It’s a make-or-break moment.
Congress now is at the midpoint of the TPA extension. Allow me to clarify: If we fail to lead, others will step in. This is America's final opportunity to do so.
Leadership on trade matters most as it enhances our well-being. Any American, regardless of their location or region, benefits. These agreements' success will notably assist manufacturers, farmers, and service industries. But all Americans thrive in a two-way, free economy.
With key players in Congress failing to agree, the rest of the world progresses. For instance, India serves as the largest target outside the TPP talks. It has reached a stage in its development where it is losing its agricultural advantage, yet it falls behind us in manufacturing. Declining alignments are crumbling as new trading partners arise.
Globalization is persisting and is changing right before our three eyes. American ought to stand at the vanguard. We clearly possess several advantages. We are the world's oldest democracy, largest economy, most stable society, most powerful military, and technological leader. While different from how other countries govern themselves, America's blend of capitalism, democracy, and individual freedoms constitutes an unmatched winning formula. Our competitors are attempting to understand our method. Sitting on the sidelines simply makes no sense. Missing this critical opportunity would be a costly mistake.
